_comment: Audit B-08 — the performance budget, measured against the four baseline URLs from B-00.
It is a regression guard, not the aspiration: the thresholds sit just below what the site
measures today, so a change that makes things worse fails the build while the current
The URLs are DIRECTORY paths, not /index.html. Loading dist/index.html at the literal
URL /index.html makes React Router match no route, so the page hydrates as the 404
(hydration mismatch in the console) and renders robots=noindex (SEO drops to 0.63).
state passes.
Mobile only, which is Lighthouse's default. Do NOT add preset:desktop here: it drops the
mobile-only SEO audits (tap-targets, font-size), so tap-targets becomes 'not a known audit'
and the SEO category scores 0.66 on a page that is otherwise perfect.
`canonical` and `is-crawlable` are off: lhci serves dist from localhost, where every
canonical points at www.alliedplumbing.ca and so looks cross-origin. Both are asserted
properly, against the real origin, by `npm run check:head`.
LCP: the audit's goal is 2,500 ms. Today the two photographic heroes measure 3.0-3.4 s
because their source images are upscaled AI-generated PNGs. Real photography (D-01) is the
fix, so the hard limit is 4,000 ms and the 2,500 ms goal is tracked in
docs/audit/open-items.md rather than failing every build until the photos exist.
Resource budgets are TRANSFER bytes, which is what Lighthouse reports, not source size.
Today: ~85 KB JS and ~10 KB CSS transferred.
JS budget: the audit asks for 150 KB transferred. The homepage ships ~181 KB, and roughly
50 KB of that is framer-motion, pulled in for a MotionConfig, one fade-up on the CTA band
and two hover scales on the residential service page. Replacing those three with CSS would
meet the target, but it changes how the site animates, so it is a design decision rather
than a build one. The limit is set at 190 KB as a regression guard; see
docs/audit/open-items.md.
